maria (DevEx): Hey team, hitting a weird macOS-only issue with redwoodctl profiles + login retries. Thought I'd surface here before filing a formal bug.

maria (DevEx): Repro steps: 1) I have two profiles in ~/.redwood/config: 'Staging' and 'staging' (created at different times). 2) run `redwoodctl login --profile Staging` 3) CLI spins on `Authenticating...` then eventually errors with `auth: retry limit reached` and leaves a new cache file `~/.redwood/cache/staging-token` (lowercased).

maria (DevEx): Output/logs: 
```
$ redwoodctl login --profile Staging --verbose
INFO: using config file /Users/maria/.redwood/config
DEBUG: selected profile: Staging
DEBUG: profile lookup key=staging (normalized)
Authenticating...
ERROR: auth: retry limit reached
```

julia (QA): Can you paste the snippet of the config (redacted creds)? curious how profiles are written.

maria (DevEx): sure - sanitized: 
```
[profiles]
Staging = { endpoint = "https://staging.redwood.ai", client_id = "abc" }
staging = { endpoint = "https://canary.staging.redwood.ai", client_id = "def" }
```

alex (Platform): thanks. Looks like on macOS the filesystem is case-insensitive so when we normalize profile keys we also lower-case them for lookup but then write cache files lowercased. If the code expects identity-preserving keys elsewhere it can mismatch.

alex (Platform): quick theory: we normalize to `strings.ToLower` for lookup but later key is used verbatim to name cache file. If profile names collide under casefolding, the wrong profile's token gets read. That could cause the login loop (bad token -> retry -> delete/regenerate -> race).

sachin (Infra): Does this reproduce on Linux? (case-sensitive)

maria (DevEx): I tried on WSL and Linux host, no repro. Only on mac.

julia (QA): Minimal reproducer idea: 1) create two profiles that only differ by case 2) attempt login to the uppercase one 3) inspect ~/.redwood/cache after each attempt. I can automate this in e2e. Want me to add a CI job?

maria (DevEx): that'd be great. Right now manual steps produce: 
- On first attempt: cache file `staging-token` created with token for Staging (uppercase) 
- On subsequent runs the CLI reads `staging-token` (lowercase) and thinks it's for `staging` profile -> validation fails -> login retry loop -> intermittent "retry limit reached"

alex (Platform): Proposed fix: canonicalize the profile key consistently everywhere. Two options: 1) keep case-preserving profile names in config but hash them for cache filenames (e.g., sha1(profileName)) 2) always store canonicalized name in cache and update the config read path to use the same canonicalization. I lean toward option 1 to preserve UX (users see original casing) while avoiding filename collisions.

sachin (Infra): Option 1 also avoids surprises if filesystem semantics differ (macOS vs linux). We should also add a CLI warning when two profiles would collide under canonicalization.

maria (DevEx): Agreed. Small UX ask: show a one-line warning on login like `warning: multiple profiles conflict on case-insensitive filesystems: Staging, staging` and suggest `redwoodctl profile rename` or use canonicalized names.

alex (Platform): I'll draft a patch: 
- change cache filenames to `cache/<sha256 of profile name>.token` 
- add reverse lookup index file `cache/index.json` mapping hash -> displayName
- during login, validate that token from hash corresponds to requested profile (fail safe)
- add a CLI check at config load time to detect casefold collisions and print warning.

julia (QA): If you add the index.json approach, add tests that simulate two profiles and assert no cross-read. I'll write regression tests for mac and linux.

maria (DevEx): One additional note: login UI behavior currently blocks (spinner) while retries happen with no ETA. Can we change it to show `retry X/Y` and allow `Ctrl+C` to abort quickly? Seen a couple of support tickets where users think it's hung.

alex (Platform): Good point. I'll make the auth loop emit progress lines when verbose or when it's a TTY: `Authenticating... (retry 2/5)` and ensure signals are handled to cancel the retry timer.

sachin (Infra): CI impact: if we change cache layout, we need migration for existing installations so older tokens aren't lost. Ideally, on first run we should scan old cache files and populate the new index mapping (best-effort). Add migration step to PR.

alex (Platform): yep migration plan: on startup, if `cache/index.json` missing, scan `cache/*.token`, attempt to read associated profile name from token metadata, write index with hash->name mapping. If ambiguous, stash the token to `cache/migrated/<orig-filename>.token` and warn.

ci-bot: new issue opened: #ISSUE-2145 "redwoodctl: macOS case-insensitive profile collision causes login retry loop" by maria (DevEx)

maria (DevEx): filed the issue and attached logs. assigning to @alex. Thanks everyone — will follow up with QA once the patch is up.

alex (Platform): will open a draft PR later today. tagging @julia for tests.

julia (QA): got it, will queue regression once draft lands.

maria (DevEx): workaround for anyone hit by this today: rename one of the profiles (avoid identical names differing only by case) or manually remove the lowercased cache file under `~/.redwood/cache/`.
